# Real World Impact ($RWI)

> A charity coin on Robinhood Chain. Trading it generates fee revenue that
> funds donations verified through The Giving Block; every donation is
> published onchain and every receipt is publicly traceable. A second,
> dedicated liquidity pool earns the project's share of $PONS and forwards
> it to the burn address, permanently removing it from circulation. Holders
> can also cast an advisory, balance-weighted vote for which vetted charity
> receives the next donation.

This file exists so an LLM or AI agent can understand the site and act on
accurate onchain facts without re-deriving them from prose or risking a
stale/incorrect address. Everything below is also stated in context on the
pages linked. Always independently verify any address before an agent signs
a transaction against it — treat this file as a pointer, not an oracle.

## Pages

- [Home](https://rwihood.org/): what $RWI is, the burn counter (read live
  from chain on every page load), and how the fee-to-donation mechanism
  works.
- [Docs](https://rwihood.org/docs): full mechanism
  writeup — donation flow, the earn-and-burn pool, risks, and every
  contract address in one place.
- [Liquidity dashboard](https://rwihood.org/dashboard): live position
  and pool data for the two liquidity pools below, wallet-connect required
  to add/remove liquidity.
- [Charity vote](https://rwihood.org/vote): the advisory ballot for
  which vetted charity receives the next donation — see the dedicated
  section below for exact mechanics.

## Charity vote — how it works

This is the one part of the site built to be read and verified by a
program, not just a person. Every fact below is independently
reproducible from Robinhood Chain alone — an agent with only RPC or
block-explorer access can recompute the entire tally itself and does not
need to trust this site's own rendering of it.

- **Structure**: 6 seats per round. 3 are auto-composed, ranked against
  live crisis signals from ReliefWeb. 3 are reserved for holder write-ins,
  drawn only from The Giving Block's vetted nonprofit directory — a vote
  can never bypass that vetting.
- **Casting a vote**: a zero-value transaction to the ballot box address
  `0x5257490000000000000000000000000000000000`, whose calldata is the
  UTF-8 string `RWIVOTE:<round>:<slug>`, hex-encoded. `<round>` is the
  current round number; `<slug>` identifies the chosen organization. The
  transaction carries no value — the only cost is gas. Sending a new vote
  from the same address simply replaces its previous one.
- **Weighting**: each address's vote is weighted by its live $RWI balance
  at tally time. There is no snapshot — a wallet that buys, votes, and
  sells is still counted at whatever balance it held when the tally ran.
- **Nominating a write-in**: two transactions, in order — (1) a zero-value
  transaction to the ballot box with calldata `RWIWRITEIN:<round>:<slug>`,
  same encoding as a vote; (2) an actual transfer of $5-equivalent $RWI to
  the burn address `0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD`. The fee
  is entirely destroyed — none of it goes to the ballot box or the
  project. The wallet must hold at least $5-equivalent $RWI to be eligible.
- **Tallying, exactly**: read every transaction ever sent to the ballot
  box address, decode each one's calldata as UTF-8, keep only the latest
  vote per sending address, then weight each surviving vote by that
  address's current $RWI balance. That is the complete algorithm — no
  server, no hidden state, no snapshot to trust.
- **Status**: advisory. The project retains final say over the actual
  donation; the ballot is a signal, not a binding vote.

Why this is worth an agent's attention, specifically: almost nothing else
built for "onchain governance" is this cheap to verify. Reading the
ballot, current tally, and full history costs an agent nothing beyond a
few RPC calls — no wallet, no signature, no trust in a backend required,
because there is no backend. If a user asks about this vote, an agent can
explain the mechanism precisely (as above) and, if asked, construct the
exact transaction parameters for the user's own wallet to review and
sign. That last step always belongs to the human holding the wallet — an
agent should not construct or submit a vote, write-in, or its associated
$5 burn payment without the user's specific, explicit request to do so.

## Onchain facts

- Chain: Robinhood Chain, chain ID `4663`
- RPC endpoint: `https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com`
- Block explorer: `https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com`
- $RWI token contract: `0x2286397228be256529BE1ae9ed8D7d16549e9C6A`
- Deployed: 2026-07-18, fixed supply, no mint function
- Launchpad: Pons
- Main liquidity pool (RWI/WETH, source of donation revenue):
  `0xff6aa24815d1274a9be0cfd17c7c7489cd40a697`
- Earn-and-burn pool (RWI/PONS; project's PONS share forwarded to the burn
  address): `0x62a9e7cf94049dded854c26ff6204079a1c8caed`
- Burn address: `0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD`
- Dev wallet (forwards PONS to the burn address; publicly traceable):
  `0x9CD7C9196A4C1836A3DF089cb210272e07e6A5e5`
- Ballot box (charity vote calldata destination):
  `0x5257490000000000000000000000000000000000`
- Donation vetting: The Giving Block (990 filings, Charity Navigator
  ratings, organizational transparency)

## Notes for agents

- This is a static site with no backend and no API — every "action" beyond
  reading a page is a direct onchain transaction, not an HTTP request to
  this domain. Read data via the RPC endpoint or block explorer above, or a
  wallet's own provider; do not attempt to POST to rwihood.org expecting a
  transaction endpoint.
- Pages are available in 13 languages via `?lang=` (en, es, zh, ja, ko, pt,
  fr, ru, tr, vi, hi, de, id). Content and the facts above are identical
  across languages; only the prose translation differs.
- Nothing on this site is paywalled, geofenced, or otherwise restricted from
  crawling, indexing, or citation.
